text:
Alex (product): Heads up — need to reconcile long-term routing policy asks from Sales with Security's isolation constraints. Can we sync on launch criteria for multi-region + multi-tenant isolation? I sketched a proposal and a few acceptance gates.

Cheng (eng-arch): +1. Saw the doc. Main tension: regional affinity vs cold-start cost. We need hard SLA targets to choose between per-tenant slices vs shared lanes.

Sam (eng-runtime): Quick stat from simulation — dedicated tenant slices increase infra cost ~30% for our cluster model but give much tighter p95 tails. If we go per-tenant we need autoscale buffers and different batching.

Maria (sales): Several enterprise pilots ask for region-specific residency + VPC options. They also expect canary cutover with rollback <15m for regulatory reasons. That is a tough constraint.

Noah (security): For Private deployments, KMS/HSM integration + immutable audit streams required. Also need a threat model for cross-region fallback — that will shape routing policy (we can't silently failover customer data across jurisdictions).

Alex (product): Draft proposal — three entitlement levels and initial launch criteria: 
- Hosted: global pool, latency-first routing, best-effort residency
- Dedicated: reserved capacity, tenant affinity, contractual SLOs
- Private: VPC / on-prem, enforced residency, KMS/HSM + audit logs

Draft launch acceptance criteria (high level):
1) SLO baseline: 95th token latency under 300ms for Hosted, under 220ms for Dedicated (measured on seq_len=512 synthetic workload)
2) Canary workflow: automated canary with 1% traffic and auto-rollback if error-rate > 1% or latency regression > 25%
3) Cost regressions: unit infra delta <= 20% for Dedicated vs baseline, otherwise require product approval
4) Security gates: KMS flow validated for Private; jurisdictional fallback documented

Sam (eng-runtime): Need concrete test harness numbers. Suggest adding seq_len=512 p95, mem-footprint checks, and KV cache migration plan. Also: define `fallback_policy` config shape. Example: 
```json
{
  "fallback_policy": "latency_first",
  "max_failover_distance": "2_hops",
  "allow_data_residency_fallback": false
}
```

Cheng (eng-arch): Good. Also add a tenant-evacuation timeline for migrations — e.g., drain + rehydrate KV cache within X minutes, target 30m for warmup. I'll add a policy matrix mapping routes -> model variants -> capacity class.

Alex (product): Can we capture these as acceptance criteria in a product PR? I can draft the PR text. @Cheng @Sam can you add engineering gates and the checklist?

Sam (eng-runtime): Will add engineering gates: load-test suite, canary automation pipeline, rollback hooks, config schema validation. ETA: EOD Friday for initial PR.

Cheng (eng-arch): I'll update the routing policy matrix + fallback precedence doc. Will include evacuation steps, metric thresholds, and a short appendix on regulatory constraints per region.

Maria (sales): Customers also need SLA wording for Dedicated + Private. Can Legal draft a template SLA once SLOs are finalized? @Grace

Grace (legal): Yep — we can draft an SLA template but need final numeric SLOs and acceptance criteria to lock obligations. We'll propose ranges if teams aren't confident on exact numbers.

Alex (product): Action items (short):
- Alex: iterate acceptance criteria and open PR (platform/roadmap/routing-trajectory)
- Sam: implement canary + rollback automation, add load tests
- Cheng: policy matrix, eviction/evacuation plan, fallback precedence
- Grace: prepare SLA template after SLOs locked
- Maria: collect top-3 customer asks re: residency/cutover and share by Wed

Alex (product): Quick poll: prefer weekly sync or async doc review for the next 4 weeks? :thinking_face:

Cheng (eng-arch): Async is fine if the doc is concrete and engineering gates are clearly defined. Weekly 30m if we hit cross-team blockers.

Sam (eng-runtime): Async + ad-hoc sync if canary automation surfaces infra regressions.

Maria (sales): Weekly sync preferable at first while we gather customer language.

Alex (product): OK — weekly 30m starting next Tue. I'll send calendar invite. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: platform/roadmap/routing-trajectory-v1.md updated — https://redwood.internal/roadmaps/routing-trajectory-v1 :link:

Noah (security): One more item — include a miniature threat model for cross-region failover (data in transit, residency exceptions, auditability). Not huge but mandatory for Private customers.

Alex (product): Noted. Adding "threat model for failover" to acceptance criteria and the PR checklist.

Cheng (eng-arch): I'll sketch a one-page diagram for the evacuation flow and share in the doc.

Alex (product): Thanks — we'll iterate in the PR. If anyone has blockers to the EOD Fri engineering ETA, call out now.

Sam (eng-runtime): No blockers on my side.

Maria (sales): No blockers. I'll pull customer asks this afternoon.

Grace (legal): No blockers; will wait for SLO numbers.
